review_notes: I read the whole file and searched for repeated proof blocks. I checked the CharP and Row8OddAt helper uses and the card_statedClassicalModel_two signature. The most repeated blocks are the (n : K) ≠ 0 arguments (3 copies) and the leaf9 skeleton (6 copies). The `p < p^2` calc and the `p^2 ∣ card` derivations repeat too, but they are short, so I did not report them. I did not check that the proposed rewrites compile. The leaf9 finding is weaker because the model lemmas and projection indices differ per case.

findings.excerpt: have := (CharP.cast_eq_zero_iff Kf q.p 2).1 (by simpa using h0)
findings.problem: The same argument is written out three times. If a prime r differs from the characteristic ℓ of a field, then (r : K) ≠ 0. Each copy rewrites with CharP.cast_eq_zero_iff and then applies Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq. The copies are the `hne` block in row8OddItem_zero (about lines 56-60) and the two `h2` blocks in row8OddItem_one (lines 84-88 and 91-100). The second `h2` block also needs an extra `hℓ` rewrite, because the characteristic is stated in terms of ValidLieTypeIndex.characteristic. Mathlib already has the lemma that does exactly this.
findings.proposed_change: Replace each block with the existing lemma `CharP.cast_ne_zero_of_ne_of_prime`. For example `have h2 : (2 : Kf) ≠ 0 := CharP.cast_ne_zero_of_ne_of_prime Kf Nat.prime_two (Ne.symm hq2)` for the first branch, and `hne := CharP.cast_ne_zero_of_ne_of_prime _ hp hpr` (with the direction of the inequality adjusted) in row8OddItem_zero. In the twistedA branch, supply a `CharP` instance for the field with characteristic `ValidLieTypeIndex.characteristic ⟨.twistedA 2 q, hv⟩`, or rewrite via `hℓ`, and apply the same lemma. This would be a lemma use rather than a new lemma. The CharP instance on GaloisField q.p _ is assumed to be available in all three cases; I did not verify the twistedA case.
findings.benefit: This removes about 15 lines of repeated divisibility reasoning. Each non-vanishing fact becomes one line that cites a named Mathlib lemma, so the proofs can be read and kept up to date more easily.

evidence.excerpt:
lemma cast_ne_zero_of_ne_of_prime [Nontrivial R]
    {p q : ℕ} [CharP R p] (hq : q.Prime) (hneq : p ≠ q) : (q : R) ≠ 0
rw [CharP.cast_eq_zero_iff (GaloisField q.p q.exponent) q.p p] at h0

findings.problem: Six proofs share the same skeleton after `Row8OddAt.of_card`. They destructure `hX` as ⟨q, hq2, hq1, hv, ⟨e0⟩⟩, obtain a StatedClassicalModel from a per-family lemma, substitute the parameters with `rw [hq2, hq1] at hmod`, rewrite the cardinality with one projection of `card_statedClassicalModel_two`, and close with `decide +kernel`. Only the model lemma and the projection index (.1, .2.1, .2.2.1, .2.2.2.1) differ. The `of_card` interface forces this inline repetition for every leaf. The `Row8OddAt.of_card` argument list `(N := …) S (by norm_num) (by decide +kernel) (by decide +kernel)` is also repeated each time.
findings.proposed_change: Add a helper such as `Row8OddAt.of_statedModel_two`. Its hypotheses would be a tag `t`, numbers `n` and `f`, `hmodel : ∀ X [Group X] [Finite X], P X → StatedClassicalModel X t n 2 f`, and `hord : the matching order formula = N`. The conclusion would be `Row8OddAt P`, given `hN`, `hS`, `h2` as in `of_card`. Its proof applies `of_card` and rewrites with the appropriate `card_statedClassicalModel_two` conjunct for `t`. The leaf proofs would then only give the model lemma. For example, leaf9_zero would provide `fun X _ _ hX => by obtain ⟨q,hq2,hq1,hv,⟨e0⟩⟩ := hX; simpa [hq2,hq1] using statedClassicalModel_of_isoLie_A hv e0`. The ordering and projection selection would be centralised in one place.
findings.benefit: The shared reduction (obtain parameters, substitute, select cardinality formula, evaluate) is written once. Adding or auditing a leaf would then only involve its model lemma and the numeric data. The six copies could no longer drift apart, for example through a wrong projection index. This is a weaker finding than the first: the per-case model lemmas differ, and part of the repetition is routine plumbing.
